How does a smart water meter turn flowing water into the number on its screen?

Fig 3 · Inside the meter

    Stopwatch0.0000 µswaiting for a click
    Arrivals, zoomed in (µs)
    • speed = head start × c² ÷ (2 × mirror gap) = 214.6 ns × (1482 m/s)² ÷ (2 × 60 mm) = 3.93 m/s
    • flow = speed × hole = 3.93 m/s × 176.7 mm² = 0.694 L every second
    • total = 1234.5675 m³ + 0.000694 m³ = 1234.5682 m³, shown as 1234.568

    The click is 1 MHz sound, far too high to hear: its crests are 1.48 mm apart, and each wiggle in the zoom is one millionth of a second. In the slow-motion pings the water stands still, because it moves only 0.20 mm while the click crosses.

    Meter colour

    The big idea: sound arrives sooner going with the water, and that tiny head start tells the meter how fast the water flows.

    Where the numbers come from
    • Transit times on a U path with two 45° reflectors: tdown = l/c + L/(c + v) + l/c and tup = l/c + L/(c − v) + l/c with l = D/2, so Δt = tup − tdown = 2Lv/(c² − v²) ≈ 2Lv/c², and Q = K·v·A: TI SNIA020, Ultrasonic Sensing for Water Flow Meters and Heat Meters. The figure uses the exact form and solves it for v; it takes K = 1 (real meters calibrate K for the flow profile).
    • c = 1482.4 m/s: speed of sound in pure water at 20 °C from Marczak's equation (J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 102, 1997), one of the fits on NPL's speed-of-sound guide. Tap water is close to this; a real meter corrects for temperature.
    • DN15, Q3 = 2.5 m³/h (Q4 = 3.125 m³/h), transit-time ultrasonic measurement, an optical eye on the front and a 3.65 V lithium battery for up to 16 years: Kamstrup MULTICAL 21 / flowIQ 2101 EU type-examination certificate DK-0200-MI001-015.
    • 1 MHz transducers, one upstream and one downstream measurement per second, and absolute times of flight of 35–70 µs in typical meters: TI TIDM-1019 reference design. The 50.5 µs here sits inside that range.
    • Assumed, not from a datasheet: the 60 mm between the mirrors (chosen to fit a ~110 mm DN15 body and give a time of flight in TI's range), a round 15 mm bore (many meters narrow the tube to speed the water up, which makes Δt bigger), a 3-cycle burst, an AA-size lithium cell, the 1234.5675 m³ starting total and the shape of the received wave in the zoom. Change any of them in model.mjs and every number follows.
    • 8-0:1.0.0: the water volume register that the probe reads in Fig 1 (same caveat as there: the rest of the code and the total are invented for these figures).
    • The water streaks are drawn about 281 times slower than real water so you can follow them; in the two pings they move at the true speed slowed 100000 times, which is 0.20 mm in a whole trip, so they stand still.
